title: What is Sanatan Dharma?
summary: Sanatan Dharma is a broad civilizational and spiritual tradition rather than a single-creed system. It includes Vedic and Agamic traditions, many schools of philosophy, devotional paths, yoga, ritual, ethics, sacred narratives and regionally diverse practices.
body: The significance of What is Sanatan Dharma? is broader than its short popular description. Reading it alongside the foundational ideas, ways of life and spiritual paths within Sanatan traditions shows how the topic fits into thought, practice and historical tradition. The sections below expand that setting in a clear, structured way without reducing a diverse tradition to a single formula.

title: Dharma
summary: Dharma is a central Indian concept whose meaning changes with context: sustaining order, ethical responsibility, appropriate conduct, duty, law or the characteristic nature of a thing. Hindu texts therefore discuss dharma at personal, social, political and spiritual levels.
body: A useful way to study Dharma is to begin with its core meaning and then connect it with the foundational ideas, ways of life and spiritual paths within Sanatan traditions. That turns the topic from a standalone fact into part of a larger intellectual and cultural landscape. This page follows that approach with a concise but substantial explanation.

title: Karma
summary: Karma literally means action. In Hindu philosophical traditions it also refers to the moral and causal significance of actions and intentions, especially when discussing character, rebirth and liberation. Karma is not simply “fate”; action, choice and discipline remain important.

title: Atman
summary: Atman refers to the deepest self or principle of selfhood in many Hindu philosophical traditions. The Upanishads made inquiry into Atman central, while later Vedanta schools developed different explanations of its relation to Brahman, Ishvara and the world.

summaryHi: आत्मन् अनेक हिंदू दर्शनों में व्यक्ति के गहरे आत्म-स्वरूप या चेतन अस्तित्व की अवधारणा है। उपनिषदों ने आत्मन् की खोज को केंद्रीय विषय बनाया, जबकि बाद के वेदांत दर्शनों ने आत्मन्, ब्रह्मन्, ईश्वर और जगत के संबंध की अलग-अलग व्याख्याएँ कीं।
bodyHi: आत्मन् को समझने का अच्छा तरीका है कि पहले उसके मूल अर्थ को पहचाना जाए और फिर उसे सनातन परंपरा की मूल अवधारणाओं, जीवन-दृष्टि और साधना-पथों से जोड़ा जाए। ऐसा करने पर विषय अलग-थलग जानकारी न रहकर सनातन ज्ञान-परंपरा के बड़े चित्र का हिस्सा बन जाता है। यह पृष्ठ उसी संबंध को स्पष्ट, सम्मानपूर्ण और क्रमबद्ध रूप में प्रस्तुत करता है।
summaryEn: Atman refers to the deepest self or principle of selfhood in many Hindu philosophical traditions. The Upanishads made inquiry into Atman central, while later Vedanta schools developed different explanations of its relation to Brahman, Ishvara and the world.
bodyEn: A useful way to study Atman is to begin with its core meaning and then connect it with the foundational ideas, ways of life and spiritual paths within Sanatan traditions. That turns the topic from a standalone fact into part of a larger intellectual and cultural landscape. This page follows that approach with a concise but substantial explanation.

title: Brahman
summary: Brahman is the term used in the Upanishadic and Vedantic traditions for ultimate reality. Different Vedanta schools agree on its central importance but differ in how they describe its relation to the world, individual selves and the personal divine.
body: The significance of Brahman is broader than its short popular description. Reading it alongside the foundational ideas, ways of life and spiritual paths within Sanatan traditions shows how the topic fits into thought, practice and historical tradition. The sections below expand that setting in a clear, structured way without reducing a diverse tradition to a single formula.

title: Moksha
summary: Moksha means liberation from bondage and the cycle of samsara. Hindu traditions describe different paths—knowledge, devotion, disciplined action, meditation and divine grace—and disagree in detail about what the liberated state means.
body: Moksha cannot be understood fully through a one-line definition. It becomes clearer when placed within the foundational ideas, ways of life and spiritual paths within Sanatan traditions. This page therefore moves from the basic idea to its wider setting and related themes, so the reader can build a connected understanding rather than remember an isolated fact.

title: Early Upanishadic Thought
summary: Early Upanishads shifted attention from ritual alone toward questions about the self, ultimate reality, consciousness, death, rebirth and liberation. Dialogues involving teachers such as Yajnavalkya, Gargi and Maitreyi became central to later Vedanta.
body: The significance of Early Upanishadic Thought is broader than its short popular description. sections.title: A new depth of inquiry
sections.content: The early Upanishads turn ritual vocabulary inward and ask what remains constant behind changing experience, what the self is, how knowledge transforms a person, and how freedom from repeated becoming may be understood. Their dialogue form makes philosophical inquiry itself part of the teaching.
sections.contentEn: The early Upanishads turn ritual vocabulary inward and ask what remains constant behind changing experience, what the self is, how knowledge transforms a person, and how freedom from repeated becoming may be understood. title: Formation of the Epic Traditions
summary: The Ramayana and Mahabharata grew through long textual and oral transmission. They preserve narratives, ethics, political reflection, pilgrimage geography and philosophical teaching that became deeply embedded in Indian cultural memory.

summary: Dharmasutra and Dharmashastra literature systematized discussions of conduct, duties, legal procedure, inheritance, penance and social norms. Different texts emerged in different periods and never represented a single, uniform legal code for all of India.

summary: Indian philosophical schools developed rigorous debates about valid knowledge, language, causation, matter, consciousness, God, self and liberation. Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa and Vedanta became especially influential frameworks.

title: Diversification of Bhakti Movements

title: Madhva and Dvaita Vedanta

title: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library
summary: India created TKDL to document traditional knowledge in patent-searchable form so patent examiners can identify relevant prior art during examination.
body: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library is an Indian initiative for protecting documented traditional knowledge within the modern patent system. It organizes knowledge from traditions such as Ayurveda, Siddha, Unani and Yoga into searchable forms that patent examiners can consult while checking prior art. Its importance lies in making already-known knowledge visible within formal patent examination.

sections.title: Why documentation matters
sections.content: A large body of traditional knowledge existed in classical texts and Indian languages, but it was not always easy for international patent examiners to search. TKDL was created to classify, translate and organize such material so that existing knowledge can be recognized during novelty and prior-art examination.
sections.contentEn: A large body of traditional knowledge existed in classical texts and Indian languages, but it was not always easy for international patent examiners to search. TKDL was created to classify, translate and organize such material so that existing knowledge can be recognized during novelty and prior-art examination.
sections.contentHi: बहुत-सा पारंपरिक ज्ञान पुराने ग्रंथों और भारतीय भाषाओं में उपलब्ध था, लेकिन अंतरराष्ट्रीय पेटेंट-जाँच में उसे ढूँढना कठिन हो सकता था। टीकेडीएल ने इस ज्ञान को वर्गीकृत, अनुवादित और खोजयोग्य रूप में व्यवस्थित करने की दिशा में काम किया, ताकि पहले से ज्ञात विधियों पर नएपन का अनुचित दावा न किया जा सके।

sections.title: Role in patent examination
sections.content: TKDL is not a system for patenting a tradition. Its role is to make already-existing knowledge visible as prior art. In that way it supports the protection of traditional knowledge and can help patent offices identify or challenge claims that are not genuinely novel.
sections.contentEn: TKDL is not a system for patenting a tradition. Its role is to make already-existing knowledge visible as prior art. In that way it supports the protection of traditional knowledge and can help patent offices identify or challenge claims that are not genuinely novel.

title: Nakshatras: The Lunar Mansion System
titleHi: नक्षत्र: चंद्र पथ का पारंपरिक विभाजन
summary: Nakshatras are a traditional Indian division of the ecliptic, usually into 27 sectors and in some older schemes 28. They are closely connected with tracking the Moon and with calendrical traditions.

title: Navagraha: Tradition vs Modern Planets
titleHi: नवग्रह: परंपरा और आधुनिक ग्रहों का अंतर
summary: Navagraha means nine grahas in Hindu religious-astrological tradition: Surya, Chandra, Mangala, Budha, Brihaspati, Shukra, Shani, Rahu and Ketu. This is not the same category as the modern astronomical list of planets.
summaryEn: Navagraha means nine grahas in Hindu religious-astrological tradition: Surya, Chandra, Mangala, Budha, Brihaspati, Shukra, Shani, Rahu and Ketu. This is not the same category as the modern astronomical list of planets.
summaryHi: हिंदू धार्मिक-ज्योतिषीय परंपरा में नवग्रह हैं: सूर्य, चंद्र, मंगल, बुध, बृहस्पति, शुक्र, शनि, राहु और केतु। यह आधुनिक खगोल विज्ञान की ग्रह-सूची के समान श्रेणी नहीं है।

sections.title: Why the distinction matters

title: How Tithi Is Calculated
titleHi: तिथि की गणना कैसे होती है
summary: In astronomical Panchanga calculation, a tithi is based on the changing angular separation between the Moon and the Sun. A full 360° cycle is divided into 30 tithis, each spanning 12° of elongation.
summaryEn: In astronomical Panchanga calculation, a tithi is based on the changing angular separation between the Moon and the Sun. A full 360° cycle is divided into 30 tithis, each spanning 12° of elongation.
summaryHi: खगोलीय पंचांग गणना में तिथि सूर्य और चंद्रमा के बीच बदलते कोणीय अंतर पर आधारित होती है। 360° के पूरे चक्र को 30 तिथियों में बाँटा जाता है और प्रत्येक तिथि 12° के अंतर को दर्शाती है।

sections.content: Researchers recorded numerous stone anchors and submerged or intertidal structural remains, supporting the interpretation of Dwarka as an important historical harbour and maritime centre.

sections.title: Connection with Krishna tradition
sections.content: Dwarka has a deep and continuous sacred association with Krishna. Archaeology securely establishes ancient settlement and maritime activity in the region; the sacred narrative and the archaeological chronology are shown side by side.

title: Heliodorus Pillar and the Worship of Vasudeva
titleEn: Heliodorus Pillar and the Worship of Vasudeva
summary: The Heliodorus pillar at Besnagar records that Heliodorus, an ambassador associated with the Indo-Greek king Antialkidas, erected a Garuda pillar in honour of Vasudeva and identified himself as a Bhagavata. It is major epigraphic evidence for early Vasudeva-Krishna devotion.
summaryEn: The Heliodorus pillar at Besnagar records that Heliodorus, an ambassador associated with the Indo-Greek king Antialkidas, erected a Garuda pillar in honour of Vasudeva and identified himself as a Bhagavata. It is major epigraphic evidence for early Vasudeva-Krishna devotion.

sections.title: What the inscription says
sections.content: The record identifies the monument as a Garudadhvaja dedicated to Vasudeva and calls Heliodorus a Bhagavata. Because the text is inscribed on the monument itself, it is direct epigraphic evidence.
sections.contentEn: The record identifies the monument as a Garudadhvaja dedicated to Vasudeva and calls Heliodorus a Bhagavata. Because the text is inscribed on the monument itself, it is direct epigraphic evidence.

sections.title: Historical importance
sections.content: The pillar demonstrates that Vasudeva devotion was established enough in the second century BCE to receive monumental patronage and to attract a foreign-born devotee or patron.

title: 33 Koti Devata: how should the expression be understood?

title: Ahimsa, compassion and responsibility
summary: Ahimsa became a major ethical ideal across Hindu, Jain and Buddhist traditions. Hindu texts also discuss difficult cases of duty, so the ideal is interpreted through context rather than a single simplistic rule.

summaryHi: अहिंसा हिंदू, जैन और बौद्ध परंपराओं में प्रमुख नैतिक आदर्श बनी। हिंदू ग्रंथ कठिन कर्तव्य-स्थितियों पर भी विचार करते हैं, इसलिए इस आदर्श को संदर्भ सहित समझा जाता है।
